lesson_topic: The Cold War — Origins: Capitalism vs. Communism Ideological Foundations

principles.evidence: All four slides are entirely text-based; no diagrams, charts, maps, illustrations, or data figures are present in any slide. The absence of any non-decorative graphic means visual-verbal reciprocity cannot be established, and multiple concept-rich slides (e.g., ideological comparison, WWII alliance map) warranted but lack visuals.

On-screen text consists of full prose paragraphs (three complete sentences per slide), far exceeding the keyword/label threshold and requiring well over five seconds to scan. The transcript narration is verbatim or near-verbatim identical to the on-screen text across all four slides, producing full redundancy between channels with no substantive elaboration.

All detailed descriptive content is delivered as dense on-screen prose paragraphs rather than via narration over supporting graphics, inverting the intended modality split. The narration reads the on-screen text aloud verbatim on every slide, meaning the auditory channel adds no information beyond what the visual channel already presents as extended text.

No decorative imagery, tangential anecdotes, or extraneous content are present; every sentence is directly relevant to the stated ideological comparison objective. Slide backgrounds appear clean and uncluttered, and the narration is free of filler or digression, maintaining strict topical focus throughout all four segments.

No visual cues such as arrows, highlights, color contrast, or callouts are present to direct learner attention to key elements; typographic hierarchy is limited to a title and undifferentiated body text. The narration does not employ explicit verbal signals (e.g., 'notice,' 'the key point is') to orient the learner, and no single takeaway is visually or verbally emphasized per slide.

Because no graphics are present, all criteria requiring label-to-graphic proximity, integrated text, or visual connectors between terms and referents are unobservable and scored as not met. The absence of a visual channel eliminates any possibility of spatial contiguity between text and image; text blocks are isolated without a corresponding graphic unit.
